sweep.note: settled by the same syncMeeting the touch path uses; a due WAIT still needs the chair to decide (proceed/lapse/recess); no waiter deadline elapsed in this pass
sweep.expiredWaitersMeans: every waiter whose OWN deadline elapsed in this pass and was woken under the event name "deadline": `{ meeting, member, until, id, wake }`. The row state becomes "expired" (not "fired"): the event the member waited for did NOT happen, its own timeout did — the wake exists so it can re-decide instead of waiting forever. An empty array means no waiter deadline elapsed (the means line stays so the empty array is not silent).
sweep.sweptMeans: `swept` counts only the transitions THIS last pass settled; `recentTransitions` is the bounded cross-pass history, so a non-zero history beside `swept:0` means other passes or the touch path moved meetings
sweep.recentTransitionsNote: this is the BOUNDED history (last 20 transitions across all state-moving paths); each row carries its OWN passAt, which is the instant THAT transition was recorded - it is not `at`, because `at`/`swept`/`transitions` describe the last BEAT sweep only, while a meeting also moves on the touch path (attend/speak/proceed)

receipt.liveWhileArchivedMeans: only one object carries this id here (no archived record with the same name)
receipt.title: 法定人数会议
receipt.agenda: 法定人数：三席到齐后才成立（m-unanimous）。
agendaItems: 法定人数：三席到齐后才成立（m-unanimous）。
receipt.agendaItemsMeans: the SAME agenda string split on `;` `；` `、` `,` and newlines, each item trimmed, order preserved. The convene face joins an agenda ARRAY with "; ", so this is how a caller reads its items back; the STRING is the truth and this is a reading of it — a prose agenda that itself uses one of those separators will read as several items
receipt.materials: 法定人数：三席到齐后才成立（m-unanimous）。
receipt.materialsMeans: `materials` is the name this face has always used for the agenda — the ONE text line the convene face stores (an `agenda` array is joined with "; " before it lands here). It is the SAME value as `agenda` in this block; the second name exists because readers already parse `materials`, not because there is a second fact
receipt.formalAgendaItemsMeans: null: this meeting carries NO per-item formal agenda. The convene face stores the agenda as ONE text line in `materials` (an array is joined with "; ") and `formal_agenda` there is a BOOLEAN "the agenda came from a formal block" flag, not an item list — so null is the absence of an item list, NOT an empty agenda: read `agendaItems` for the items
receipt.formalAgendaItemsWhy: no per-item agenda was recorded: this meeting never declared a formal agenda, so there is no item list to read (the agenda, if one was given, is the `materials` line — read `agendaItems`)
receipt.formalAgendaItemsHint: to record a per-item formal agenda, convene the meeting AGAIN and pass an ARRAY of items through the pack door: vibe_v5_meeting { formal_agenda: ["<item>", { title: "<item>", kind: "review" }] } — that is the front door (its schema accepts a boolean OR an array), so the items are validated and stored by the pack; from the kernel face the same array is open({ formalAgenda: [...] }). A boolean (formal_agenda:true, or formalAgenda:true) only DECLARES the agenda formal and leaves the items as the materials line

procedure.note: 本类型没有推荐流程骨架（这是具名决定，不是遗漏）：框架只提供它的通用会议原语，议程由院士自行编排。

procedureProgress.means: the procedure is a RECOMMENDATION, not a gate: every field here is a COUNT of what is on record — skeletonSteps counts the steps the recommended skeleton LISTS (a property of the recommendation, not progress through it), speeches counts speech entries in the minutes, motions counts motions raised, queued counts the RAW length of the floor queue (entries, not people: it includes members who are not present and entries that never take a turn — read waitingNow for the queue entries who ARE present and can take a turn now, and queuedAbsentList for the names held in the queue without attendance), present counts seated members, and advancing is true when any of those counts is above zero. None of them is a step index: the framework never holds a meeting to a step and would have to invent one to report it

receipt.convenedByMeans: the caller of open() is the convener (no other originator is recorded)
receipt.wallLimitMeans: the meeting’s OWN upper bound, frozen at open: wallLimitMsSource "convene" = the chair set it (durationMs), "vmu.meetings.hardLimitMs" = the deployment default (`1800000` ms here); extendlimit ADDS to the current bound and reports extendedMs, and a request that would pass `vmu.meetings.extendCeilingMs` (`14400000` ms here) is refused WHOLE by name (`VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`) — nothing is clamped to the boundary, and there is no unbounded choice
receipt.speechExtendMeans: the SPEECH bound (per member), NOT the meeting's wall bound: `speeches` counts speak() calls recorded on this face and `extensions` counts action="extend" calls that GRANTED time (each one raised that member's speech budget by speechExtendMs, at most speechExtendMax times). When speechExtendMs=0 the declared step is ZERO, so an extend call grants nothing and is answered `applied:false` instead of counting here: `extensions` is a count of grants, not a duration. The meeting's OWN wall clock is wallLimitMs/extendedMs and is raised by action="extendlimit" — two different bounds, two different commands
receipt.turnsMeans: SPEECHES recorded on THIS kernel instance's copy of the meeting (speak() holds its only increment site, `m.turns += 1`); it is NOT a count of member turns — the durable `state.json` `turns` (an array of {member,turn,phase,round,at}) and `vibe_vmu_turn {op:"status"}.turns` are different counters. In a multi-kernel deployment another instance may have delivered a speech it has not written back here, so the durable archived row can hold a larger number than this reading.
receipt.speechesMeans: speeches counts accepted speech acts in this meeting; `turns` is the SAME number under its older name (kept so existing readers do not break) — a member TURN is a different thing, counted by the turn orchestrator
receipt.turnsUnattributedMeans: turns minus Σ speechUsed[].speeches on THIS face. 0 means every counted turn has a recorded speech (the normal case: an accepted speak() raises both). A number > 0 is a turn this instance counts but cannot attribute to a recorded speech — it can only come from a writer that raised `turns` without the matching speech row (another instance, or a turn counted BEFORE the speech was accepted, which the acceptance-point increment above no longer does). It is NOT subtracted from `turns` on a read: the reading says which half is unattributed instead of quietly editing the record
receipt.spokeByMeans: members with at least one recorded speech in THIS meeting (the fact; minutes() is a shaped view of it)
receipt.omittedMeans: empty on purpose: `summary()` and `vibe_vmu_meeting {action:"status"}` both spread THIS block, so neither face drops a member of the who-spoke family (speeches, turnsAccounted, turnsUnattributed and spokeBy appear on both, and speak/close receipts carry the same block). A face that has to drop one must list the key in omittedKeys and say why — a missing key is never its own explanation
receipt.rosterMeans: the roster is the INVITATION LIST of this meeting (who was convened), not the bench. rosterNarrowed:true means convene was given an explicit subset (`members`, or a non-empty `roster`) and the meeting read back exactly those members; benchSize is how many live members the deployment had when it was convened (0 = this deployment exposes no membership seam, so no narrowing can be shown). The CHAIR is seated by opening even when it is not on the list — that is why `present` can name a member outside `roster`; `attend()` later adds a member, and then the roster is the invitation PLUS the members who joined. `eligible` is who may vote: the declared voter seats (vmu.meetings.eligibleSeats) intersected with THIS meeting roster, or the whole roster when no seat rule is declared. A count cannot answer "who": these fields are the ids themselves.
receipt.eligibleMeans: who may vote here: the declared voter seats (chair, member) intersected with THIS meeting roster — a member on the bench but not invited is not eligible here

waitStates.means: seated but has not spoken yet: it is waiting for the chair to open the floor or to be asked
seated but has not spoken yet: it is waiting for the chair to open the floor or to be asked
seated but has not spoken yet: it is waiting for the chair to open the floor or to be asked

receipt.waitStatesMeans: waitStates is derived from THIS meeting own facts — its roster, its present set, its recorded speeches (minutes entries of kind "speech"), its late-admission queue and its proposed/seconded motions — never from wall-clock guessing. waitState: "spoke" = present and at least one speech recorded; "present" = seated but not yet spoken; "awaiting" = NOT seated, held at the door by lateAdmission:"chair" (the chair can admit it); "absent" = on the roster and not present. `owes` is true when the member is seated and a proposed/seconded motion has no vote from them (`owesWhat` names the motion ids). ★ WHAT WAITING IS NOT: members are NOT resident processes and this framework keeps NO timer for them — a member waiting means "the next turn belongs to somebody else", and after its turn the agent HANDS BACK to the chair. waitRecommended is advice about whether to drive a turn now, not a promise that anything will happen on its own. ★ SINCE RUN 239-D the framework DOES hold a timer and DOES wake: a member with nothing to do can register a `waiters` row (until: speak | vote | motion | poll | phase | attend-all | hand | deadline | meeting-closed, with an optional timeoutMs) and is woken when that event happens — so the sentence above keeps its meaning for `waitStates` (nobody is a resident process and a turn still ends by handing back), while `waiters` is the durable registration that replaces polling and empty turns.
receipt.waitRecommendedWhy: the house has arrived (3 present) and NO speech is recorded yet: the chair has not opened the floor — this is the moment to drive the first turn, and no member should be waiting on another member
receipt.lateAdmissionMeans: lateAdmission is THIS meeting policy for a late arrival (a late arrival is decided by vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs against openedAt): "open" seats a late member and records late:true; "chair" holds the member at the door (pendingLate) until the chair calls admit(); "refuse" refuses the late arrival by name and names the two repairs (the chair admits, or the member joins the next meeting). THE DEFAULT IS "chair": a late arrival is institutionally a request to be seated, so the chair decides it, and the hold is readable as pendingLate instead of the member slipping in unseen. "open" is the permissive policy and "refuse" the closed one; a meeting row that was opened before this default carries its own recorded value and is not retroactively changed.

receipt.waitersMeans: waiters are DURABLE rows on the meeting itself: each names the member and the EVENT it waits for (`until`), the instant it was armed and, when a timeout was given, its deadline. state: "armed" = waiting, the event has not happened yet; "fired" = the event happened and a WAKE WAS ATTEMPTED — `wake.delivered/via/woken` say whether it reached the member, so fired is a DELIVERY fact and NOT a statement that the member has acted, nor that the wake succeeded; "expired" = the deadline passed before the event (only for waits armed with timeoutMs); "cancelled" = withdrawn by unwait(), replaced by a newer wait for the same member, or dropped because the meeting closed. Read `minutes` / `motions` for what actually happened; read `waiters` for who asked to be woken and with what outcome.

waiterStatesMeans.armed: waiting: the event has not happened yet — this member may end its turn; the wake will start it again
waiterStatesMeans.fired: the event happened and a wake was ATTEMPTED for this member; check `wake.delivered` and `wake.via` (a "none" via means no seam and no mailbox existed) — fired does not mean the member acted
waiterStatesMeans.expired: the deadline it named passed before the event; the member was woken under the event name "deadline" so it can re-decide instead of waiting forever
waiterStatesMeans.cancelled: no longer waiting (withdrawn, replaced by a newer wait for the same member, or the meeting closed)

receipt.waitersBecause: `waitStates` (roster / present / held at the door) and `waiters` (event registrations) are TWO facts: waitStates says where a person stands in this meeting NOW, waiters says which EVENT would wake it. Neither is derived from the other
receipt.stateMeans: the meeting is OPEN and running: speak/vote/hand are open (this is the SERVICE vocabulary; the primitive calls the same phase in_session)
receipt.note: ★ motions/votes/state here describe the MEETING’s own ask()+answer()+motion cycle. procedureProgress.means: the procedure is a RECOMMENDATION, not a gate: every field here is a COUNT of what is on record — skeletonSteps counts the steps the recommended skeleton LISTS (a property of the recommendation, not progress through it), speeches counts speech entries in the minutes, motions counts motions raised, queued counts the RAW length of the floor queue (entries, not people: it includes members who are not present and entries that never take a turn — read waitingNow for the queue entries who ARE present and can take a turn now, and queuedAbsentList for the names held in the queue without attendance), present counts seated members, and advancing is true when any of those counts is above zero. None of them is a step index: the framework never holds a meeting to a step and would have to invent one to report it

receipt.wallLimitMeans: the meeting’s OWN upper bound, frozen at open: wallLimitMsSource "convene" = the chair set it (durationMs), "vmu.meetings.hardLimitMs" = the deployment default (`1800000` ms here); extendlimit ADDS to the current bound and reports extendedMs, and a request that would pass `vmu.meetings.extendCeilingMs` (`14400000` ms here) is refused WHOLE by name (`VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`) — nothing is clamped to the boundary, and there is no unbounded choice
receipt.speechExtendMeans: the SPEECH bound (per member), NOT the meeting's wall bound: `speeches` counts speak() calls recorded on this face and `extensions` counts action="extend" calls that GRANTED time (each one raised that member's speech budget by speechExtendMs, at most speechExtendMax times). When speechExtendMs=0 the declared step is ZERO, so an extend call grants nothing and is answered `applied:false` instead of counting here: `extensions` is a count of grants, not a duration. The meeting's OWN wall clock is wallLimitMs/extendedMs and is raised by action="extendlimit" — two different bounds, two different commands
receipt.turnsMeans: SPEECHES recorded on THIS kernel instance's copy of the meeting (speak() holds its only increment site, `m.turns += 1`); it is NOT a count of member turns — the durable `state.json` `turns` (an array of {member,turn,phase,round,at}) and `vibe_vmu_turn {op:"status"}.turns` are different counters. In a multi-kernel deployment another instance may have delivered a speech it has not written back here, so the durable archived row can hold a larger number than this reading.
receipt.speechesMeans: speeches counts accepted speech acts in this meeting; `turns` is the SAME number under its older name (kept so existing readers do not break) — a member TURN is a different thing, counted by the turn orchestrator
receipt.turnsUnattributedMeans: turns minus Σ speechUsed[].speeches on THIS face. 0 means every counted turn has a recorded speech (the normal case: an accepted speak() raises both). A number > 0 is a turn this instance counts but cannot attribute to a recorded speech — it can only come from a writer that raised `turns` without the matching speech row (another instance, or a turn counted BEFORE the speech was accepted, which the acceptance-point increment above no longer does). It is NOT subtracted from `turns` on a read: the reading says which half is unattributed instead of quietly editing the record
receipt.spokeByMeans: members with at least one recorded speech in THIS meeting (the fact; minutes() is a shaped view of it)
receipt.omittedMeans: empty on purpose: `summary()` and `vibe_vmu_meeting {action:"status"}` both spread THIS block, so neither face drops a member of the who-spoke family (speeches, turnsAccounted, turnsUnattributed and spokeBy appear on both, and speak/close receipts carry the same block). A face that has to drop one must list the key in omittedKeys and say why — a missing key is never its own explanation
receipt.votesNote: this meeting records no motion votes and no minutes vote events HERE. A decision taken through the BALLOT BOX is not a motion: read the box face (boxstatus / the boxclose receipt) for its tally
receipt.closureTallyMeans: the closure tally is the INSTITUTE-LEVEL unanimity reading (`vibe_vmu_vote`, read back at `vibe_vmu_status { detail: "closure" }`), and it is a DIFFERENT record from this meeting board: the votes are cast as institute votes, so `present`/`motions`/`votes` above record NO vote events for them. votesCast here next to an empty motion list is two records, not two truths
receipt.closureAccountMeans: no as-of-close account was ever frozen for this meeting: the closure reading is only the LIVE one (closureTally), and a later vote changes it
receipt.rulingsNotOnThisBoard: this board records ATTENDANCE (`present`, which is also the quorum denominator) and SPEECH (`transcript`), and it does NOT record RULINGS: a member files its verdict as a CARD (`vibe_v5_verdict`), and the chair aggregates those cards with `vibe_v5_verdict_final`, whose receipt answers `coverage`, `sources{ n, submitted, typed }` and `attribution`. A member can file a ruling without taking a seat, and can take a seat without filing anything — so "present:1 with an empty transcript" beside "two rulings submitted" is two records (a seat and a card), not two truths, and neither can be computed from the other

receiptMeta.note: NOTHING was elided by us: this receipt is over MAX_TOOL_RESULT_BYTES (12000) but no string leaf exceeded 2000, and meeting the budget would require dropping content, which would change its shape. `originalBytes` is the real size. The HOST may insert its own `[...]` marker (hostElision) - that one is outside this receipt.

receipt.noticesMeans: notified / notifyRows / notifyFailed are the kernel open() receipt fields, passed through unchanged (the kernel wrote the durable rows, so there is exactly ONE row per invited member and ONE notice line): `notified` names the members that really got a row, `notifyRows` names the mail ids, `notifyFailed` names every member that did not with the kernel reason. receipt.typeMeans: `type` decides the PROCEDURE (which skeleton this meeting follows) and is the word the institute uses; `kind` is the meeting BOARD label (sync/division/verify-request/solve-vote) and is what an archive files the row under. When no kind was passed the label is DERIVED from the type where the type names one (debate→verify-request, closure→solve-vote, division→division) and `kindSource:"derived-from-type"` says nobody chose it; a type with no natural label falls back to "sync" with `kindSource:"default"`. Either way it is a filled-in label, not a reading of what the meeting was
receipt.kindSourceMeans: no kind was passed: the framework filed this meeting under its default kind "sync". The label is legal but nobody chose it — pass kind (sync/division/verify-request/solve-vote) or title to name the meeting yourself
receipt.rosterMeans: the roster is the INVITATION LIST of this meeting (who was convened), not the bench. rosterNarrowed:true means convene was given an explicit subset (`members`, or a non-empty `roster`) and the meeting read back exactly those members; benchSize is how many live members the deployment had when it was convened (0 = this deployment exposes no membership seam, so no narrowing can be shown). The CHAIR is seated by opening even when it is not on the list — that is why `present` can name a member outside `roster`; `attend()` later adds a member, and then the roster is the invitation PLUS the members who joined. `eligible` is who may vote: the declared voter seats (vmu.meetings.eligibleSeats) intersected with THIS meeting roster, or the whole roster when no seat rule is declared. A count cannot answer "who": these fields are the ids themselves.
receipt.atSourceMeans: the caller gave an ABSOLUTE time (epoch ms, numeric string or ISO-8601); at/scheduledFor is that instant in epoch ms
receipt.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
receipt.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). TWO instants are in play and they are NOT the same fact: `openedAt` is the ATTENDANCE BASELINE (the due time, i.e. scheduledFor, fixed when the meeting was scheduled) and `activatedAt` is when the meeting REALLY became runnable (the touch that completed the attendance rule, or the chair proceed). A scheduled meeting that had to wait therefore has openedAt earlier than activatedAt, and `startedLate` says so; `lateReads.openedAt` on an attend receipt is the baseline, and null while the meeting has not started
receipt.lateAdmissionMeans: lateAdmission is THIS meeting policy for a late arrival (a late arrival is decided by vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs against openedAt): "open" seats a late member and records late:true; "chair" holds the member at the door (pendingLate) until the chair calls admit(); "refuse" refuses the late arrival by name and names the two repairs (the chair admits, or the member joins the next meeting). THE DEFAULT IS "chair": a late arrival is institutionally a request to be seated, so the chair decides it, and the hold is readable as pendingLate instead of the member slipping in unseen. "open" is the permissive policy and "refuse" the closed one; a meeting row that was opened before this default carries its own recorded value and is not retroactively changed.
receipt.wallLimitNote: the meeting’s OWN upper bound, frozen at open: `wallLimitMs` is the value, `wallLimitMsSource` says who froze it (`convene` = the chair set it with durationMs, `vmu.meetings.hardLimitMs` = the deployment default), and `extendlimit` can raise it later: extensions ADD to the current bound, and a request that would pass `vmu.meetings.extendCeilingMs` (this deployment declares no value, so the runtime ceiling applies; the refusal itself prints the ceiling it used, as `after / ceiling`) is refused BY NAME (`VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`) — nothing is clamped to the boundary. `extendCeilingMs` is the ceiling in effect for THAT refusal.
receipt.sequenceMeans: the meetings after this one were declared IN THIS CALL: `index` is this meeting's position (0-based), `total` counts it, and `next` is the SEQUENCE ROW of the meeting that follows (`{type,kind,subject}` - the declaration, not an id: an id exists only once that meeting is actually convened, and the driver takes the row, convenes it, and reads the new id from the open receipt; null = last). Advancing is decided by the call that declared them, not by a settings key, so `enforced` names no policy for it.
receipt.note: the original could also PROPOSE a meeting from a non-chair seat and let the chair convene it; this face has no propose path (named gap: procedure/propose). ★★ THIS FACE ONLY CONVENES: for status/summary/snapshot/close/extend/extendlimit/proceed/lapse/ballot/speak/hand/hands/order/invite/invitedspeak/attend/flow/overrideorder use vibe_vmu_meeting { action, id } - the kernel face, which reaches the same meeting object. Measured on a full live run: an agent tried summary/close HERE, got nothing, and reported it as a missing capability; the capability existed one face over and nothing said so. ★ D9 邀请面 (this round): hand/invite/invitedspeak/order/attend now really reach a SERVICE meeting through that face — hand = a member queues itself, invite = the CHAIR puts one member or an ordered list (members:[…]) on the floor queue, order = reads the real queue back, invitedspeak = the invited voice speaks in the minutes, attend = marks a member present (an invitation NEVER marks anybody present: attendance is its own act and only it counts for the quorum). silent/end/hands stay primitive-only and the kernel face refuses them on a service meeting BY NAME. ★ A floor-order override (flow/overrideorder) still needs vmu.meetings.orderMode declared by the deployment; v5r does not declare it, so on a real run it is refused by name rather than silently ignored. ★ The recommended procedure is a RECOMMENDATION: skipping it, reordering it, or ignoring it entirely is allowed and unchecked.
receipt.callerIsSeatMeans: this key answers ONE question: did this call run from the named seat and its own session? It does not say whether the seat carried the act out - that is what a delivered turn (turnReceipts, deliveryPath) answers
receipt.ranInOwnTurnMeans: true when this call ran from the seat own session, or when the kernel reported that a turn for this seat was actually DELIVERED and returned (out.turnDelivered) - the two facts that one key used to conflate
receipt.memberActedMeans: this call ran from the OFFICE (a root session, which is not a seat) and named member "r-acad": the record was written IN THAT SEAT'S NAME, but the seat did not act in its own turn. `memberActed:false` states that difference - orchestrating on a seat's behalf is not the same act as carrying it out, and a reader who needs the seat's own judgement should ask for it in a turn of that seat

receipt.message: late arrival refused by this meeting policy: "r-1" is 120000ms past openedAt and lateAdmission is "refuse" (vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs=1)
receipt.hint: TWO REPAIRS, and neither is a retry of attend(): (a) the CHAIR may admit the member with admit({ meeting: "m13", member: "r-1", actor: "<chair id>" }) — that is a chair decision recorded as admittedBy/admittedAt; (b) the member joins the NEXT meeting. Retrying attend() under "refuse" will refuse again.
receipt.memberActedMeans: member "r-1" was NAMED by a call that ran from member "r-1", and this call was REFUSED (`VMU_LATE_ADMISSION_REFUSED`): nothing was recorded in that seat's name and the seat did not act in its own turn — a refusal receipt records who TRIED, which is precisely what a refund of the act must not erase (the named seat is the caller here, yet the refusal means the seat did nothing: the attempt failed before any act)

receipt.arrivalMeans: TWO readings of the same room, printed by name: roster presence is "how many of the invited members are in the room", electorate presence is "how many of the members this meeting actually waits for are in the room" — the opening rule uses `opensOn` (electorate), and `missing` names the members still missing from THAT set
receipt.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
receipt.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). receipt.lateMeans: NOT LATE: at 1800000000000 this arrival is 0 ms past openedAt 1800000000000, within vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs=1 (the threshold is measured from openedAt, not from the first arrival)

quorum.presentNote: present = chair (seated by open(), so the house can transact at all) + members who attended or voted; presentBreakdown splits them, and `unanswered` names who has done neither
quorum.metIs: the FLOOR question only (present >= required) — it is NOT the institution rule; with required=0 it is true while nobody has attended. Read unanimity.met / the pack rule for the real threshold

receipt.turnsMeans: SPEECHES recorded on THIS kernel instance's copy of the meeting (speak() holds its only increment site, `m.turns += 1`); it is NOT a count of member turns — the durable `state.json` `turns` (an array of {member,turn,phase,round,at}) and `vibe_vmu_turn {op:"status"}.turns` are different counters. In a multi-kernel deployment another instance may have delivered a speech it has not written back here, so the durable archived row can hold a larger number than this reading.
receipt.speechesMeans: speeches counts accepted speech acts in this meeting; `turns` is the SAME number under its older name (kept so existing readers do not break) — a member TURN is a different thing, counted by the turn orchestrator
receipt.turnsUnattributedMeans: turns minus Σ speechUsed[].speeches on THIS face. 0 means every counted turn has a recorded speech (the normal case: an accepted speak() raises both). A number > 0 is a turn this instance counts but cannot attribute to a recorded speech — it can only come from a writer that raised `turns` without the matching speech row (another instance, or a turn counted BEFORE the speech was accepted, which the acceptance-point increment above no longer does). It is NOT subtracted from `turns` on a read: the reading says which half is unattributed instead of quietly editing the record
receipt.spokeByMeans: members with at least one recorded speech in THIS meeting (the fact; minutes() is a shaped view of it)
receipt.omittedMeans: empty on purpose: `summary()` and `vibe_vmu_meeting {action:"status"}` both spread THIS block, so neither face drops a member of the who-spoke family (speeches, turnsAccounted, turnsUnattributed and spokeBy appear on both, and speak/close receipts carry the same block). A face that has to drop one must list the key in omittedKeys and say why — a missing key is never its own explanation
receipt.budgetWhy: no meeting budget was crossed and none is declared (vmu.meetings.budgetTurns/budgetTokens/budgetWallMs are 0, or their thresholds were not reached) — budget:null means "no verdict", not "plenty left"

speechBound.why: no speech-time bound is declared (vmu.meetings.speechDefaultMs=0 and vmu.meetings.speechMaxMs=0): ms:0 means UNBOUNDED, not "zero time"

queueRead.means: the effective order is [r-1, r-2] and the turn is held among the PRESENT waiters [r-1, r-2]: an absent member ahead of you does not hold the floor (they would be refused `attend() first` anyway); a member who is NOT in the queue at all speaks as a slip (position:null, slipped:true), never as a turn

A count cannot answer "who": these fields are the ids themselves.
receipt.eligibleMeans: who may vote here: the declared voter seats (chair, member) intersected with THIS meeting roster — a member on the bench but not invited is not eligible here

waitStates.means: seated but has not spoken yet: it is waiting for the chair to open the floor or to be asked
seated and has spoken at least once (the speech row is in minutes)

receipt.waitStatesMeans: waitStates is derived from THIS meeting own facts — its roster, its present set, its recorded speeches (minutes entries of kind "speech"), its late-admission queue and its proposed/seconded motions — never from wall-clock guessing. waitState: "spoke" = present and at least one speech recorded; "present" = seated but not yet spoken; "awaiting" = NOT seated, held at the door by lateAdmission:"chair" (the chair can admit it); "absent" = on the roster and not present. `owes` is true when the member is seated and a proposed/seconded motion has no vote from them (`owesWhat` names the motion ids). ★ WHAT WAITING IS NOT: members are NOT resident processes and this framework keeps NO timer for them — a member waiting means "the next turn belongs to somebody else", and after its turn the agent HANDS BACK to the chair. waitRecommended is advice about whether to drive a turn now, not a promise that anything will happen on its own. ★ SINCE RUN 239-D the framework DOES hold a timer and DOES wake: a member with nothing to do can register a `waiters` row (until: speak | vote | motion | poll | phase | attend-all | hand | deadline | meeting-closed, with an optional timeoutMs) and is woken when that event happens — so the sentence above keeps its meaning for `waitStates` (nobody is a resident process and a turn still ends by handing back), while `waiters` is the durable registration that replaces polling and empty turns.
receipt.waitRecommendedWhy: no member is waiting right now: 2 member(s) have already spoken and no floor request is queued
receipt.lateAdmissionMeans: lateAdmission is THIS meeting policy for a late arrival (a late arrival is decided by vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs against openedAt): "open" seats a late member and records late:true; "chair" holds the member at the door (pendingLate) until the chair calls admit(); "refuse" refuses the late arrival by name and names the two repairs (the chair admits, or the member joins the next meeting). THE DEFAULT IS "chair": a late arrival is institutionally a request to be seated, so the chair decides it, and the hold is readable as pendingLate instead of the member slipping in unseen. "open" is the permissive policy and "refuse" the closed one; a meeting row that was opened before this default carries its own recorded value and is not retroactively changed.

arrival.opensOnMeans: the touch that OPENS this meeting is judged on the ELECTORATE (roster minus the seats vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats forbids to attend), not on the roster: a member who cannot attend cannot ever "arrive", so waiting for one would be waiting forever
arrival.means: TWO readings of the same room, printed by name: roster presence is "how many of the invited members are in the room", electorate presence is "how many of the members this meeting actually waits for are in the room" — the opening rule uses `opensOn` (electorate), and `missing` names the members still missing from THAT set

receipt.arrivalMeans: TWO readings of the same room, printed by name: roster presence is "how many of the invited members are in the room", electorate presence is "how many of the members this meeting actually waits for are in the room" — the opening rule uses `opensOn` (electorate), and `missing` names the members still missing from THAT set
receipt.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
receipt.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). TWO instants are in play and they are NOT the same fact: `openedAt` is the ATTENDANCE BASELINE (the due time, i.e. scheduledFor, fixed when the meeting was scheduled) and `activatedAt` is when the meeting REALLY became runnable (the touch that completed the attendance rule, or the chair proceed). A scheduled meeting that had to wait therefore has openedAt earlier than activatedAt, and `startedLate` says so; `lateReads.openedAt` on an attend receipt is the baseline, and null while the meeting has not started
receipt.waitersMeans: waiters are DURABLE rows on the meeting itself: each names the member and the EVENT it waits for (`until`), the instant it was armed and, when a timeout was given, its deadline. state: "armed" = waiting, the event has not happened yet; "fired" = the event happened and a WAKE WAS ATTEMPTED — `wake.delivered/via/woken` say whether it reached the member, so fired is a DELIVERY fact and NOT a statement that the member has acted, nor that the wake succeeded; "expired" = the deadline passed before the event (only for waits armed with timeoutMs); "cancelled" = withdrawn by unwait(), replaced by a newer wait for the same member, or dropped because the meeting closed. Read `minutes` / `motions` for what actually happened; read `waiters` for who asked to be woken and with what outcome.

waiterStatesMeans.armed: waiting: the event has not happened yet — this member may end its turn; the wake will start it again
waiterStatesMeans.fired: the event happened and a wake was ATTEMPTED for this member; check `wake.delivered` and `wake.via` (a "none" via means no seam and no mailbox existed) — fired does not mean the member acted
waiterStatesMeans.expired: the deadline it named passed before the event; the member was woken under the event name "deadline" so it can re-decide instead of waiting forever
waiterStatesMeans.cancelled: no longer waiting (withdrawn, replaced by a newer wait for the same member, or the meeting closed)

receipt.waitersBecause: `waitStates` (roster / present / held at the door) and `waiters` (event registrations) are TWO facts: waitStates says where a person stands in this meeting NOW, waiters says which EVENT would wake it. Neither is derived from the other
receipt.stateMeans: the meeting is OPEN and running: speak/vote/hand are open (this is the SERVICE vocabulary; the primitive calls the same phase in_session)
receipt.note: ★ motions/votes/state here describe the MEETING’s own ask()+answer()+motion cycle. A member answering a vibe_vmu_turn prompt is a DIFFERENT loop: read vibe_vmu_turn’s receipts (awaiting/memberPrompt/deliveryPath) for that one. hasDeliverSeam on the primitive face refers to open({deliver}), not to the turn loop’s deliveryPath.
receipt.rulingsNotOnThisBoard: this board records ATTENDANCE (`present`, which is also the quorum denominator) and SPEECH (`transcript`), and it does NOT record RULINGS: a member files its verdict as a CARD (`vibe_v5_verdict`), and the chair aggregates those cards with `vibe_v5_verdict_final`, whose receipt answers `coverage`, `sources{ n, submitted, typed }` and `attribution`. A member can file a ruling without taking a seat, and can take a seat without filing anything — so "present:1 with an empty transcript" beside "two rulings submitted" is two records (a seat and a card), not two truths, and neither can be computed from the other

receiptMeta.note: NOTHING was elided by us: this receipt is over MAX_TOOL_RESULT_BYTES (12000) but no string leaf exceeded 2000, and meeting the budget would require dropping content, which would change its shape. `originalBytes` is the real size. The HOST may insert its own `[...]` marker (hostElision) - that one is outside this receipt.

receipt.extendMeans: a SPEECH extension (action="extend"): a call that GRANTED time raised THIS member's speech budget by `ms`, bounded by speechExtendMax/speechMaxMs, and is readable as `extensions` on summary()/status(). `applied` says whether this call granted anything: with vmu.meetings.speechExtendMs=0 (the default) a call that names a duration grants 0 ms and answers applied:false with ms:0 — an ok:true there is NOT a raise. It never moved the meeting's wall clock — that bound is wallLimitMs/extendedMs and only action="extendlimit" moves it
receipt.appliedMeans: applied:false — this call granted NO speech time. vmu.meetings.speechExtendMs=0 here, so the step this deployment declares is 0 ms: the request would have added 0 ms, and it is reported as a no-op instead of a successful extension (extensions stays 0). The per-member speech budget cannot be raised on this deployment; the MEETING wall clock is a different bound and is raised by action="extendlimit".

receipt.memberActedMeans: this call ran from the OFFICE (a root session, which is not a seat) and named member "r-acad": the record was written IN THAT SEAT'S NAME, but the seat did not act in its own turn. `memberActed:false` states that difference - orchestrating on a seat's behalf is not the same act as carrying it out, and a reader who needs the seat's own judgement should ask for it in a turn of that seat

receipt.firedWaitersMeans: every waiter THIS call fired, with the delivery of its wake: `{ member, until, id, wake }`. receipt.archivedMeans: the record left the service live table and is held by the service ARCHIVE; `summary`/`status` read it back by id
receipt.subjectGateMeans: the debate-subject verdict stored with the meeting when it was CONVENED — the close receipt repeats it so a closer does not have to make a second call; reading cannot change it

closureVote.windowMeans: the map is this orchestrator's, but every vote is also written to the durable fold key "closure_votes", so it spans the INSTITUTE. `missing` means "no recorded judgement" this reading can see; a member who voted in ANOTHER session IS visible here through that fold
closureVote.rulingReading: NOT here: cast/votesCast are the CLOSURE vote; the DEBATE ruling is `vibe_v5_verdict_final`
closureVote.castMeaning: cast === confirmed: every enfranchised member judged it solved; NOT "votes were cast" — see votesCast for arrivals
closureVote.notEligibleMeans: members who judged but hold no closure-vote permission: recorded, neither counted nor listed as missing
closureVote.votersMeans: who voted, one row per member, the LATEST judgement wins
closureVote.reason: every enfranchised member judged the question solved

receipt.readForMeetingMeans: `closureVote.meetingId` is null BY DESIGN: the tally is INSTITUTE-WIDE (one durable key, latest-wins), not a per-meeting ballot, so it carries no meeting id of its own. readForMeeting names the meeting whose CLOSE this reading was taken for — the same tally is read at every close of the institute
receipt.closureVoteAsOfMeans: the instant the closureVote numbers above were computed; this close does NOT freeze the reading — a vote cast after it changes the same durable record, so quote closureVote + closureVoteAsOf together as the as-of-close account
receipt.countedMeans: counted answers ONE question: did the CLOSURE reading hold any vote at the instant of this close. It is NOT a condition of the close (the close passed the rails in `enforced`): counted=false means nobody had voted on "is this solved" yet, so quote closureVote.missing for who to ask — a close is not a unanimous judgement

closureVoteFrozen.means: this row is the as-of-close closure reading: 3 vote(s) cast, cast=true, confirmed=true, missing=[]. It is a RECORD, not a live view: later votes change `vibe_vmu_status { detail: "closure" }` and never this row, so quote it when the question is "what did the institute decide at close"
closureVoteFrozen.readingMeans: a later reader can compare: `vibe_vmu_status { detail: "closure" }` = the current latest-wins reading; this row = the reading at the instant of the close. Two different questions, two different answers, both honest
closureVoteFrozen.gatingMeans: freezing is bookkeeping: it does not decide the close and the close does not decide the vote

receipt.closureVoteFrozenMeans: the as-of-close closure reading is now a durable record (rec-1) on the `state` track; later votes change the live reading and never this row
receipt.closureVoteNote: closureVote (cast/confirmed/votesCast/missing) is the SEPARATE unanimity reading over the same INSTANCE, not a requirement of this close and not changed by it: this close passed the rails named in `enforced` (vmu.meetings.closeRequiresChair, vmu.meetings.confirmPreviousMinutes, vmu.meetings.committeeReportRequired, vmu.meetings.minutesActionsRequired) while the closure vote reads cast=true, confirmed=true, missing=[] — so "closed" does not mean "unanimously judged solved", and a member named in `missing` is who to ask before claiming closure. THE VOTES ARE CAST THROUGH `vibe_vmu_vote` AT THE INSTITUTE LEVEL, so the meeting board (`present`, `motions`, `votes`) records NO vote events for them: a chair who sees votesCast=3 next to an empty motions list is reading two different records, not two different truths. ★ Closing does NOT freeze this reading: it is the durable, latest-wins record (closureVoteAsOf names the instant it was read), so a vote cast after this close changes what a later reader sees while the numbers in THIS receipt stay the as-of-close account
receipt.callerIsSeatMeans: this key answers ONE question: did this call run from the named seat and its own session? It does not say whether the seat carried the act out - that is what a delivered turn (turnReceipts, deliveryPath) answers
receipt.ranInOwnTurnMeans: true when this call ran from the seat own session, or when the kernel reported that a turn for this seat was actually DELIVERED and returned (out.turnDelivered) - the two facts that one key used to conflate
receipt.memberActedMeans: this call ran from the OFFICE (a root session, which is not a seat) and named member "r-acad": the record was written IN THAT SEAT'S NAME, but the seat did not act in its own turn. `memberActed:false` states that difference - orchestrating on a seat's behalf is not the same act as carrying it out, and a reader who needs the seat's own judgement should ask for it in a turn of that seat
receipt.firedWaitersMeans: every waiter THIS call fired, with the delivery of its wake: `{ member, until, id, wake }`. Fired is a DELIVERY fact, not a promise that the member acted: vmu.meetings.wakeFailurePolicy decides what a failed wake means and the event is NEVER rolled back because a wake failed. The array is empty when no waiter was waiting for this event (the means line stays, so an empty array is not silent).

receipt.recordMeans: this is the RECORD BODY (what was said, voted and refused), not the board: `summary` is the agenda/motions view and `status` the state machine. Archived meetings stay readable here (a closed meeting keeps its minutes)
receipt.archivedMeans: this meeting is ARCHIVED (closed): its minutes are FROZEN history, and the candidate flag `archivable` is deliberately NOT printed here — a "candidate for archiving" means nothing about a record that is already archived
receipt.note: minutes are OWNED by 08/07 — this view only shapes and prunes them (a pruned entry is counted)

receipt.recordMeans: this is the VERBATIM transcript, which is pruned by its own declared setting (dropped lines are counted); `minutes` is the structured record and does not depend on it
receipt.note: capture is ENABLED (vmu.meetings.verbatimEnabled) but this meeting recorded NO verbatim line: the transcript only receives what is spoken with { verbatim: true }. The words that WERE said are on `minutes` entries (`text`), which this setting does not govern

receipt.stateMeans: the meeting is closed: its tally is frozen and its vote detail is hidden
receipt.archivedMeans: the meeting is closed and lives in the service archive: `summary` carries its motions and votes; `list` reports live and archived ids separately
receipt.hint: read the record with { action: "summary", id: "m10" }

receipt.liveWhileArchivedMeans: only one object carries this id here (no archived record with the same name)
receipt.stateMeans: the meeting is closed: its tally is frozen and its vote detail is hidden
receipt.title: 法定人数会议
receipt.rosterMeans: the roster is the INVITATION LIST of this meeting (who was convened), not the bench. rosterNarrowed:true means convene was given an explicit subset (`members`, or a non-empty `roster`) and the meeting read back exactly those members; benchSize is how many live members the deployment had when it was convened (0 = this deployment exposes no membership seam, so no narrowing can be shown). The CHAIR is seated by opening even when it is not on the list — that is why `present` can name a member outside `roster`; `attend()` later adds a member, and then the roster is the invitation PLUS the members who joined. `eligible` is who may vote: the declared voter seats (vmu.meetings.eligibleSeats) intersected with THIS meeting roster, or the whole roster when no seat rule is declared. A count cannot answer "who": these fields are the ids themselves.
receipt.eligibleMeans: who may vote here: the declared voter seats (chair, member) intersected with THIS meeting roster — a member on the bench but not invited is not eligible here

waitStates.means: seated but has not spoken yet: it is waiting for the chair to open the floor or to be asked
seated but has not spoken yet: it is waiting for the chair to open the floor or to be asked
seated but has not spoken yet: it is waiting for the chair to open the floor or to be asked

receipt.waitStatesMeans: waitStates is derived from THIS meeting own facts — its roster, its present set, its recorded speeches (minutes entries of kind "speech"), its late-admission queue and its proposed/seconded motions — never from wall-clock guessing. waitState: "spoke" = present and at least one speech recorded; "present" = seated but not yet spoken; "awaiting" = NOT seated, held at the door by lateAdmission:"chair" (the chair can admit it); "absent" = on the roster and not present. `owes` is true when the member is seated and a proposed/seconded motion has no vote from them (`owesWhat` names the motion ids). ★ WHAT WAITING IS NOT: members are NOT resident processes and this framework keeps NO timer for them — a member waiting means "the next turn belongs to somebody else", and after its turn the agent HANDS BACK to the chair. waitRecommended is advice about whether to drive a turn now, not a promise that anything will happen on its own. ★ SINCE RUN 239-D the framework DOES hold a timer and DOES wake: a member with nothing to do can register a `waiters` row (until: speak | vote | motion | poll | phase | attend-all | hand | deadline | meeting-closed, with an optional timeoutMs) and is woken when that event happens — so the sentence above keeps its meaning for `waitStates` (nobody is a resident process and a turn still ends by handing back), while `waiters` is the durable registration that replaces polling and empty turns.
receipt.waitRecommendedWhy: no member is waiting right now: 0 member(s) have already spoken and no floor request is queued
receipt.lateAdmissionMeans: lateAdmission is THIS meeting policy for a late arrival (a late arrival is decided by vmu.meetings.lateAfterMs against openedAt): "open" seats a late member and records late:true; "chair" holds the member at the door (pendingLate) until the chair calls admit(); "refuse" refuses the late arrival by name and names the two repairs (the chair admits, or the member joins the next meeting). THE DEFAULT IS "chair": a late arrival is institutionally a request to be seated, so the chair decides it, and the hold is readable as pendingLate instead of the member slipping in unseen. "open" is the permissive policy and "refuse" the closed one; a meeting row that was opened before this default carries its own recorded value and is not retroactively changed.

arrival.opensOnMeans: the touch that OPENS this meeting is judged on the ELECTORATE (roster minus the seats vmu.meetings.attendDeniedSeats forbids to attend), not on the roster: a member who cannot attend cannot ever "arrive", so waiting for one would be waiting forever
arrival.means: TWO readings of the same room, printed by name: roster presence is "how many of the invited members are in the room", electorate presence is "how many of the members this meeting actually waits for are in the room" — the opening rule uses `opensOn` (electorate), and `missing` names the members still missing from THAT set

receipt.arrivalMeans: TWO readings of the same room, printed by name: roster presence is "how many of the invited members are in the room", electorate presence is "how many of the members this meeting actually waits for are in the room" — the opening rule uses `opensOn` (electorate), and `missing` names the members still missing from THAT set
receipt.requiresChairProceedMeans: false: the meeting is already running — proceed() has nothing left to open; act in it (speak/vote/hand)
receipt.startReadsMeans: startsInMs is non-null ONLY while the meeting has not started (positive = the start time is still in the future, negative = it is overdue); elapsedSinceMs is non-null ONLY once it has started (>= 0, measured from the moment it ACTUALLY opened, i.e. activatedAt — not from scheduledFor); elapsedMs is an alias of elapsedSinceMs kept for old readers (null while not started, never negative). TWO instants are in play and they are NOT the same fact: `openedAt` is the ATTENDANCE BASELINE (the due time, i.e. scheduledFor, fixed when the meeting was scheduled) and `activatedAt` is when the meeting REALLY became runnable (the touch that completed the attendance rule, or the chair proceed). A scheduled meeting that had to wait therefore has openedAt earlier than activatedAt, and `startedLate` says so; `lateReads.openedAt` on an attend receipt is the baseline, and null while the meeting has not started
receipt.waitersMeans: waiters are DURABLE rows on the meeting itself: each names the member and the EVENT it waits for (`until`), the instant it was armed and, when a timeout was given, its deadline. state: "armed" = waiting, the event has not happened yet; "fired" = the event happened and a WAKE WAS ATTEMPTED — `wake.delivered/via/woken` say whether it reached the member, so fired is a DELIVERY fact and NOT a statement that the member has acted, nor that the wake succeeded; "expired" = the deadline passed before the event (only for waits armed with timeoutMs); "cancelled" = withdrawn by unwait(), replaced by a newer wait for the same member, or dropped because the meeting closed. Read `minutes` / `motions` for what actually happened; read `waiters` for who asked to be woken and with what outcome.

waiterStatesMeans.armed: waiting: the event has not happened yet — this member may end its turn; the wake will start it again
waiterStatesMeans.fired: the event happened and a wake was ATTEMPTED for this member; check `wake.delivered` and `wake.via` (a "none" via means no seam and no mailbox existed) — fired does not mean the member acted
waiterStatesMeans.expired: the deadline it named passed before the event; the member was woken under the event name "deadline" so it can re-decide instead of waiting forever
waiterStatesMeans.cancelled: no longer waiting (withdrawn, replaced by a newer wait for the same member, or the meeting closed)

receipt.waitersBecause: `waitStates` (roster / present / held at the door) and `waiters` (event registrations) are TWO facts: waitStates says where a person stands in this meeting NOW, waiters says which EVENT would wake it. Neither is derived from the other
receipt.agenda: 法定人数：三席到齐后才成立（m-unanimous）。
agendaItems: 法定人数：三席到齐后才成立（m-unanimous）。
receipt.agendaItemsMeans: the SAME agenda string split on `;` `；` `、` `,` and newlines, each item trimmed, order preserved. The convene face joins an agenda ARRAY with "; ", so this is how a caller reads its items back; the STRING is the truth and this is a reading of it — a prose agenda that itself uses one of those separators will read as several items
receipt.materials: 法定人数：三席到齐后才成立（m-unanimous）。
receipt.materialsMeans: `materials` is the name this face has always used for the agenda — the ONE text line the convene face stores (an `agenda` array is joined with "; " before it lands here). It is the SAME value as `agenda` in this block; the second name exists because readers already parse `materials`, not because there is a second fact
receipt.formalAgendaItemsMeans: null: this meeting carries NO per-item formal agenda. The convene face stores the agenda as ONE text line in `materials` (an array is joined with "; ") and `formal_agenda` there is a BOOLEAN "the agenda came from a formal block" flag, not an item list — so null is the absence of an item list, NOT an empty agenda: read `agendaItems` for the items
receipt.formalAgendaItemsWhy: no per-item agenda was recorded: this meeting never declared a formal agenda, so there is no item list to read (the agenda, if one was given, is the `materials` line — read `agendaItems`)
receipt.formalAgendaItemsHint: to record a per-item formal agenda, convene the meeting AGAIN and pass an ARRAY of items through the pack door: vibe_v5_meeting { formal_agenda: ["<item>", { title: "<item>", kind: "review" }] } — that is the front door (its schema accepts a boolean OR an array), so the items are validated and stored by the pack; from the kernel face the same array is open({ formalAgenda: [...] }). A boolean (formal_agenda:true, or formalAgenda:true) only DECLARES the agenda formal and leaves the items as the materials line
receipt.subjectGateMeans: no subject gate verdict was recorded for this meeting (the face that convened it recorded none)

procedure.note: 本类型没有推荐流程骨架（这是具名决定，不是遗漏）：框架只提供它的通用会议原语，议程由院士自行编排。

procedureProgress.means: the procedure is a RECOMMENDATION, not a gate: every field here is a COUNT of what is on record — skeletonSteps counts the steps the recommended skeleton LISTS (a property of the recommendation, not progress through it), speeches counts speech entries in the minutes, motions counts motions raised, queued counts the RAW length of the floor queue (entries, not people: it includes members who are not present and entries that never take a turn — read waitingNow for the queue entries who ARE present and can take a turn now, and queuedAbsentList for the names held in the queue without attendance), present counts seated members, and advancing is true when any of those counts is above zero. None of them is a step index: the framework never holds a meeting to a step and would have to invent one to report it

receipt.wallLimitMeans: the meeting’s OWN upper bound, frozen at open: wallLimitMsSource "convene" = the chair set it (durationMs), "vmu.meetings.hardLimitMs" = the deployment default (`1800000` ms here); extendlimit ADDS to the current bound and reports extendedMs, and a request that would pass `vmu.meetings.extendCeilingMs` (`14400000` ms here) is refused WHOLE by name (`VMU_RESOURCE_BUDGET`) — nothing is clamped to the boundary, and there is no unbounded choice
receipt.speechExtendMeans: the SPEECH bound (per member), NOT the meeting's wall bound: `speeches` counts speak() calls recorded on this face and `extensions` counts action="extend" calls that GRANTED time (each one raised that member's speech budget by speechExtendMs, at most speechExtendMax times). When speechExtendMs=0 the declared step is ZERO, so an extend call grants nothing and is answered `applied:false` instead of counting here: `extensions` is a count of grants, not a duration. The meeting's OWN wall clock is wallLimitMs/extendedMs and is raised by action="extendlimit" — two different bounds, two different commands
receipt.turnsMeans: SPEECHES recorded on THIS kernel instance's copy of the meeting (speak() holds its only increment site, `m.turns += 1`); it is NOT a count of member turns — the durable `state.json` `turns` (an array of {member,turn,phase,round,at}) and `vibe_vmu_turn {op:"status"}.turns` are different counters. In a multi-kernel deployment another instance may have delivered a speech it has not written back here, so the durable archived row can hold a larger number than this reading.
receipt.speechesMeans: speeches counts accepted speech acts in this meeting; `turns` is the SAME number under its older name (kept so existing readers do not break) — a member TURN is a different thing, counted by the turn orchestrator
receipt.turnsUnattributedMeans: turns minus Σ speechUsed[].speeches on THIS face. 0 means every counted turn has a recorded speech (the normal case: an accepted speak() raises both). A number > 0 is a turn this instance counts but cannot attribute to a recorded speech — it can only come from a writer that raised `turns` without the matching speech row (another instance, or a turn counted BEFORE the speech was accepted, which the acceptance-point increment above no longer does). It is NOT subtracted from `turns` on a read: the reading says which half is unattributed instead of quietly editing the record
receipt.spokeByMeans: members with at least one recorded speech in THIS meeting (the fact; minutes() is a shaped view of it)
receipt.omittedMeans: empty on purpose: `summary()` and `vibe_vmu_meeting {action:"status"}` both spread THIS block, so neither face drops a member of the who-spoke family (speeches, turnsAccounted, turnsUnattributed and spokeBy appear on both, and speak/close receipts carry the same block). A face that has to drop one must list the key in omittedKeys and say why — a missing key is never its own explanation

motions.text: 本场会议通过会议机制清单。

receipt.votesNote: this counts MOTION votes (and, failing that, minutes vote events); a BALLOT-BOX decision is a different record — read it on the ballot face (boxstatus / the boxclose receipt)
receipt.closureTallyMeans: the closure tally is the INSTITUTE-LEVEL unanimity reading (`vibe_vmu_vote`, read back at `vibe_vmu_status { detail: "closure" }`), and it is a DIFFERENT record from this meeting board: the votes are cast as institute votes, so `present`/`motions`/`votes` above record NO vote events for them. votesCast here next to an empty motion list is two records, not two truths
receipt.closureAccountMeans: the DURABLE as-of-close closure account written by `close` (rec-N on the `state` track): its numbers are frozen, so they are what the institute decided AT CLOSE even if later votes moved the live reading
receipt.rulingsNotOnThisBoard: this board records ATTENDANCE (`present`, which is also the quorum denominator) and SPEECH (`transcript`), and it does NOT record RULINGS: a member files its verdict as a CARD (`vibe_v5_verdict`), and the chair aggregates those cards with `vibe_v5_verdict_final`, whose receipt answers `coverage`, `sources{ n, submitted, typed }` and `attribution`. A member can file a ruling without taking a seat, and can take a seat without filing anything — so "present:1 with an empty transcript" beside "two rulings submitted" is two records (a seat and a card), not two truths, and neither can be computed from the other

receiptMeta.note: NOTHING was elided by us: this receipt is over MAX_TOOL_RESULT_BYTES (12000) but no string leaf exceeded 2000, and meeting the budget would require dropping content, which would change its shape. `originalBytes` is the real size. The HOST may insert its own `[...]` marker (hostElision) - that one is outside this receipt.

receipt.recordMeans: this is the RECORD BODY (what was said, voted and refused), not the board: `summary` is the agenda/motions view and `status` the state machine. Archived meetings stay readable here (a closed meeting keeps its minutes)
